evidence.conclusion_or_fact: JCR single-chain anti-hTfR antibody + CNS-protein fusion: US9994641B2 (priority 2013-12-25) claims an scFv recognizing hTfR epitopes SEQ ID NOs:1-3 and a C-terminal fusion with a CNS-acting protein (e.g., iduronate-2-sulfatase I2S), enabling BBB transport for CNS/lysosomal storage disease (Hunter/Hurler encephalopathy).
evidence.reviewer_action: Verify granted US claims and CN/EP national-phase status; check JCR product pipeline links.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: Ossianix TfR-1-selective shark VNAR nanobody platform: US11918647B2 (priority 2014-11-14) claims VNAR single-domain moieties selectively binding human TfR-1 (apical domain aa 215-380) without blocking transferrin binding and without substantially binding TfR-2, with pH-dependent reversible binding and endocytosis; VNAR-Fc fusions and TfR1/BACE1 bispecifics deliver payloads across the BBB or GI tract.
evidence.reviewer_action: Verify granted US claims and CN/EP national-phase status.

evidence.conclusion_or_fact: Dyne muscle-targeting complexes: US11795234B2 / US11839660B2 (base priority 2018-08-02; antibody branch priority 2021-07-09) claim anti-TfR1 antibodies covalently linked to oligonucleotide payloads (DUX4/DMD/DMPK-targeting ASO/gapmer/RNAi/PMO) via cleavable linkers, delivering payloads to muscle (and brain) for FSHD/DMD/DM1; antibodies bind apical TfR epitope, do not inhibit transferrin binding, and are cross-reactive human+NHP.

aliases: iron-refractory iron deficiency anemia (IRIDA) TFRC context

disambiguation_notes: TfR1 = transferrin receptor 1 (gene TFRC, protein CD71), a type-II transmembrane homodimer that binds holo-transferrin and mediates cellular iron uptake and receptor-mediated transcytosis (e.g., across the BBB).
Distinguish from TfR2 (gene TFR2, liver/erythroid iron sensing) and from the ligand transferrin (TF); patent searches must separate 'transferrin receptor' hits that only concern the ligand.

Pathways relevant to the patent landscape: iron uptake, proliferating-cell/tumor targeting, antibody/bispecific-mediated brain delivery, antibody-drug conjugates, immunoliposomes/particles, diagnostics.
The abbreviation 'TfR' (without a number) in most biomedical texts refers to TfR1/CD71; treat 'transferrin receptor' as ambiguous but likely TfR1 unless TFR2/TfR2 is explicitly named.
unresolved_questions: Confirm whether the user's focus is TfR1 biology broadly or a specific modality (antibody, BBB-shuttle, conjugate, diagnostic).
Verify official legal status in CNIPA and USPTO Patent Center for all representative families; Google Patents mirrors are screening signals only.
Separate anti-TfR1 platform patents from patents that merely mention TfR1/CD71 in a list of targets.
